cleanIntro: This guide follows Springfield Armory's Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual. That book covers the Model 2020 line as a whole and never prints "Redline", so check your variant against it. The strip is three moves: safety on, magazine out, bolt back and out past the bolt stop. Springfield then shows how to take the bolt itself apart, and where the two stock screws go back to, at a stated torque.

steps.title: Glasses on, muzzle safe, safety to S
steps.action: This guide follows Springfield's Model 2020 manual, which does not name the Redline, so check your variant against it. Eye protection first, muzzle somewhere harmless, finger off the trigger, and the safety selector to 'S'. The book puts these in that order before the magazine even comes out.
steps.quote: Always use proper eye protection when cleaning firearms.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIPPING (printed p.26, per Figure 26-1 on the page)
steps.warn: POINT GUN IN SAFE DIRECTION WHILE KEEPING FINGER OFF THE TRIGGER.

steps.title: Magazine out and the rifle proved unloaded
steps.action: Drop the magazine and unload the rifle, then look into the chamber to confirm it is empty. A round left in the chamber still fires with the magazine out, which is exactly what the book's capitalised warning is about.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIPPING (printed p.26, per Figure 26-1 on the page)
steps.warn: ALWAYS REMEMBER THE FIREARM IS ABLE TO FIRE WITH OR WITHOUT THE MAGAZINE IN PLACE.

steps.title: Adjustable cheek piece off first, if the rifle has one
steps.action: If your rifle has an adjustable cheek piece, take it off before the bolt comes back. If the stock has no adjustable cheek piece, there is nothing to do here.
steps.quote: Remove the cheek piece if rifle is equipped with an adjustable cheek piece (See Know Your Firearm Section).
steps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIPPING (printed p.26, per Figure 26-1 on the page)

steps.title: Bolt fully back
steps.action: Lift the bolt handle and draw the bolt all the way to the rear. The bolt stop only releases it from the rearmost position.
steps.quote: Retract the bolt to its most rearward position.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIPPING (printed p.26, per Figure 26-1 on the page)

steps.title: Press the REAR of the bolt stop and draw the bolt out
steps.action: Press the rear surface of the bolt stop and pull the bolt straight out to the rear. It is the rear face of the stop that releases the bolt. That is the field strip for routine cleaning.
steps.quote: Depress the rear surface of the bolt stop and remove the bolt rearward (Figure 261).
steps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIPPING (printed p.26, per Figure 26-1 on the page)
steps.warn: Never allow live ammunition in the area while you are maintaining your firearm.

steps.title: Barrel from the chamber to the muzzle, ejection port down
steps.action: Lay the barrelled action horizontally with the ejection port facing down so solvent runs out rather than into the action, and always clean from the chamber end toward the muzzle. Push the brush fully out of the muzzle before pulling it back, because reversing a brush in the bore can jam it.
steps.quote: NOTE: Barrel should lay horizontally with the ejection port facing downward during cleaning. Always clean the barrel from the chamber to the muzzle.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — CLEANING THE BARREL (PDF p.34; this edition prints no page folios)
steps.warn: You cannot change direction of the brush when brush is in the bore as this can jam the brush in the bore.

steps.title: Patch until clean, then oil, then a dry patch
steps.action: Push a solvent-soaked jag and patch through, a fresh patch each time, until a patch comes out with no fouling. Then one oiled patch, and one clean dry patch behind it to take the excess oil back out of the bore.
steps.quote: Repeat using a new patch each time, until the patch no longer shows fouling present.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — CLEANING THE BARREL (PDF p.34; this edition prints no page folios)

steps.title: Oil the bolt ways and the rear faces of the lugs
steps.action: Springfield lists the lubrication points as the bolt body, the bolt ways inside the receiver, and the rear faces of the bolt locking lugs. Grease does not go in the bore of the bolt body or on the firing pin or its spring.
steps.quote: Inside of the receiver in the bolt ways (Figure 32-2), and rear faces of the bolt locking lugs (Figure 32-3).
steps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — LUBRICATION POINTS (printed p.32, per Figures 32-1 to 32-3)
steps.warn: NOTE: Do not use grease in the bore of the bolt body or on the firing pin or spring.

deepSteps.title: Shroud forward 1/8", handle pressed in, shroud released
deepSteps.action: With the bolt out of the rifle, push the shroud toward the front of the bolt about an eighth of an inch and hold it there while you press the bolt handle inward, then let the shroud go. Doing it in that order is what lets the assembly come apart.
deepSteps.quote: Compress the shroud towards the front of the bolt 1/8” and while maintaining pressure, Press the handle inward, (Figure 29-1) then release the pressure on the shroud (Figure 29-2).
deepSteps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — BOLT DISASSEMBLY (printed p.29, per Figures 29-1 to 29-4)
deepSteps.warn: If you disassemble your Springfield Armory® firearm, do so properly.

deepSteps.title: Firing pin assembly out as one piece
deepSteps.action: Lift the firing pin assembly out of the bolt body as a unit. Springfield does not take the firing pin assembly itself apart, and neither does this guide.
deepSteps.quote: The firing pin assembly can now be removed (Figure 29-3).
deepSteps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — BOLT DISASSEMBLY (printed p.29, per Figures 29-1 to 29-4)

deepSteps.title: Bolt handle off the body, and that is the end of it
deepSteps.action: Take the bolt handle off the bolt body. Springfield's bolt disassembly stops here: no further disassembly is required.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the bolt handle from the bolt body (Figure 29-4). No further disassembly is required. Bolt disassembly is now complete.
deepSteps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — BOLT DISASSEMBLY (printed p.29, per Figures 29-1 to 29-4)

deepSteps.title: Parts solvent-cleaned, rinsed, dried and inspected
deepSteps.action: Clean the bolt parts with a powder solvent, rinse, dry and look them over before anything goes back together. Lubricate the bolt lightly and wipe the excess away.
deepSteps.quote: Clean all parts with a quality powder solvent, rinse, dry and inspect. Lightly lubricate the bolt, wipe away any excess lubricant.
deepSteps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — BOLT DISASSEMBLY (printed p.29, per Figures 29-1 to 29-4)
deepSteps.warn: NOTE: Do not use grease in the bore of the bolt body or on the firing pin or spring.

deepSteps.title: Receiver flushed with the stock off
deepSteps.action: For a full receiver clean, take the two stock screws out with a 3/16 hex drive, lift the stock away from the receiver and trigger assembly, spray the inside of the receiver with an aerosol action cleaner and let it dry. Going back, the longer screw is the rear one, the forward screw is tightened first, and neither goes past 65 in-lbs.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the 2 stock screws with a 3/16 Hex drive (Figure 27-1).
deepSteps.cite: Springfield Armory Model 2020 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — CLEANING THE RECEIVER (printed p.27, per Figure 27-1 on the page)
deepSteps.warn: NOTE: Tighten the forward screw first followed by the rear. Do not exceed 65in lbs.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Correct-caliber brush and solvent, chamber to muzzle, ejection port facing down
Brush passes fully out of the muzzle before it comes back
Fresh solvent patch each pass until no fouling shows
One oiled patch, then one clean dry patch

cleaning.name: BOLT & RECEIVER
tasks: Wipe the bolt body and lightly oil it
Light oil in the bolt ways and on the rear faces of the locking lugs
⛔ No grease in the bore of the bolt body, on the firing pin or on its spring
Thin coat of oil on the outside of the barrel and action with a soft cloth

reassembly: Bolt handle into the bolt body from the top, extractor to the right; it only goes in one way.
Bolt handle over-inserted into the bolt body.
Firing pin assembly into the bolt body in the orientation shown in the book.
Shroud compressed 1/8" while the bolt handle is pushed flush with the bolt body, then the shroud released.
Shroud oriented as shown in the book, and the bolt installed in the action.
Cheek piece back on if it was removed.
If the stock was off: action and screws back in, the longer screw at the rear, the forward screw tightened first, neither past 65 in-lbs.
Function check before any live ammunition.
fncheck: Rifle empty, magazine out, muzzle in a safe direction. Work the bolt several times and check it runs, locks and unlocks without binding. With the safety at 'S' the trigger must not fire the rifle. Springfield's warning is plain: improper disassembly or assembly creates unsafe conditions. If anything did not go back the way it came out, take the rifle to a competent gunsmith or call Springfield before shooting it.
